title: Build expression trees by precedence
description: You can follow how parser tiers build tuples for arithmetic expressions.

steps.description: lex splits the input into token pairs and appends EOF. A tree node uses an operator and two children.
The parser stores tokens and a position. peek reads the current token, while advance also moves forward.
parse_expr collects terms around addition or subtraction. parse_term collects primary expressions around multiplication or division.
An opening parenthesis sends parsing back through parse_expr. Otherwise this demonstration makes a NUM leaf from the next token.

steps.question: For 2 + 3 * 4, which operator becomes the root?
steps.answer: Addition becomes the root. The right term contains the multiplication of 3 and 4.

steps.description: show_tree prints each operator above its children. The first two displayed trees show how parentheses change the root from + to *.
